title: Contextual release pruner and variant signal hash
author: Maya Patel
description: Problem: onboarding pages and release notes for model variants accumulate many low-signal items that hide deployment risks. This PR implements a contextual release pruner that selects a small, high-signal subset of changelog fragments and pairs it with a compact variant signal hash — a deterministic, size-bounded digest derived from sampled telemetry features — to help reviewers and downstream tools quickly assess runtime affinity. Key ideas: (1) Variant signal hash condenses anonymized telemetry-derived features (sequence length distribution quantiles, common token-prefixes, average KV cache hit hint) into a stable 64-char hex digest. The hash is produced from deterministic sketching of reservoir-sampled telemetry aggregates so it is reproducible across uploads and small enough for manifests. (2) Release pruner ranks candidate changelog fragments by a hybrid score (telemetry-weighted impact + semantic novelty) and applies a length and redundancy-aware pruning pass to produce a 3-item short summary and optional extended list. Implementation details: sketches and hash generation live in registry/lib/signals/hash_sketch.go; pruning engine is in services/release/pruner.go with a preview REST endpoint at api/release_preview.go. The uploader CLI gained --publish-short-release to enable the pruned output; the registry UI shows both short and full views. Privacy and safety: telemetry inputs are pre-aggregated, bucketed, and clipped; no raw traces are exported. Backwards compatibility: new fields are additive; older clients ignore short_release and variant_signal_hash. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind feature_flags.release_pruner, internal pilot for two weeks, then opt-in for partners. Metrics from pilot: reviewer acceptance rate for onboarding briefs rose from 68% to 91% and average onboarding read-time decreased by 40%.
